reconcile.note: Clarke harmonizes the penalties by intent: Leviticus 15:24's seven-day impurity covers an unwitting encounter, while Leviticus 20:18's karet penalty covers willful intercourse.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen documents the Holiness Code's stricter personal-purity demands than earlier priestly law, a shift of which this harsher penalty is one instance.

quotes.text: Stricter demands are also made on the laity for personal holiness, especially as regards continence from the sins of the flesh, and the marriage of relatives (Leviticus xviii. xx.).
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the Law of Holiness's stricter purity demands versus earlier priestly law.

sides.verseText: \"'If any man lies with her, and her monthly flow is on him, he shall be unclean seven days; and every bed whereon he lies shall be unclean.

sides.verseText: \"'If a man lies with a woman having her monthly period, and uncovers her nakedness; he has made naked her fountain, and she has uncovered the fountain of her blood: and both of them shall be cut off from among their people.
